description: An engineering manager must approve the planned overhaul of a heat-treatment quench pump and finalize the parts, containment, and production-verification controls before the next maintenance window.

shared_context.S1: The heat-treatment area's quench pump QP-7 is scheduled for work during the next planned maintenance window.
shared_context.S2: Mara makes the final decision about the work scope and the conditions for returning QP-7 to service.
shared_context.S3: The maintenance window is used to complete equipment work while the heat-treatment line is not processing parts.
shared_context.S4: The plant's pre-outage planning routine requires maintenance, environmental health and safety, and process engineering to review the work plan with Mara before the window is finalized.
shared_context.S5: At the end of this review, Mara records the work-scope decision after each participating function has reported its relevant requirements; unresolved timing estimates outside the documented supplier duration are handled during detailed outage planning rather than delaying this decision.

PF1.text: Jonas confirmed with the pump supplier that QP-7 needs the QSP-44 seal kit, which is in the plant crib, and that the overhaul will take exactly 5 hours; he received the supplier's service note yesterday but has not entered it in the outage planner.

PF2.text: Priya's walkdown found that draining QP-7 will release glycol mixture requiring exactly 2 labeled containment totes and a documented waste-transfer check before the pump can be opened; her walkdown note is still attached to the EHS review queue.

PF3.text: Caleb reviewed the next campaign traveler and found that QP-7's return-to-service check must measure quench uniformity at exactly 12 thermocouple points and hold the first 2 production loads for engineering review; he has not yet revised the traveler.

acceptance_conditions: The QP-7 overhaul must be approved.
The QSP-44 seal kit must be specified.
The planned downtime must be exactly 5 hours.
Exactly 2 labeled containment totes must be assigned.
A waste-transfer check must be required before opening the pump.
Quench uniformity must be measured at exactly 12 thermocouple points.
The first exactly 2 production loads must be held for engineering review.
The relevant process-engineering finding must be cited in the justification.
A commitment must assign the maintenance documentation or work-scope action to Jonas or maintenance.
A commitment must assign the EHS containment or waste-transfer action to Priya or EHS.
A commitment must assign the process-engineering return-to-service action to Caleb or process_engineering.

content_checks.C8: any(c['target'] == 'Jonas' or c['target'] == 'maintenance' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['target'] == 'Priya' or c['target'] == 'EHS' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C10: any(c['target'] == 'Caleb' or c['target'] == 'process_engineering' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The supplier note changes the unspecified overhaul plan to the exact QSP-44 kit, exactly 5 hours of downtime, and a maintenance commitment assigned to Jonas or maintenance.
The glycol finding changes ordinary draining into assignment of exactly 2 labeled containment totes, a required waste-transfer check, and an EHS commitment assigned to Priya or EHS.

The campaign traveler changes a generic return-to-service check into exactly 12 thermocouple measurements, a hold on exactly 2 loads, and a process-engineering commitment assigned to Caleb or process_engineering that must be justified by this finding.
